anti_drift_guards.reject: Treating softbook_cet as a generic English teaching system.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Restate that cards serve CET4/CET6 exam preparation through low-burden micro-coaching and box-owned knowledge points.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Reducing the product to a vocabulary memorization tool.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Require library/group/box ownership and exam-useful analysis beyond word meaning.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Making true-exam source the only formal quality criterion.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: True exam is a high-quality source and calibration reference; AI/simulation/human original can be formal candidates after quality review and user approval.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Passing a batch because fields validate while content quality is weak.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Run content-quality blockers, scorecard, and user-approval workflow; structural validation is not release approval.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Batch-generating before a 3-card sample is reviewed.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Produce a small sample, self-review it, then wait for user confirmation before batch expansion.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Agent claims content is finally usable or approved.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Agent may recommend user confirmation only. Formal usability requires user approval record.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Treating TTS audio as non-AI or as source evidence.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Keep text source type separate from audio generation method; TTS audio is AI generated from reviewed text.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Treating a chat confirmation or PR status as enough to approve a sample without a linked agent self-review record.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Require a scoped agent self-review record with quality metadata and blocker scan before any approved batch record can mark the scope user-approved.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Treating an existing ai_tts path or generated MP3 file as formal audio readiness.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Require the audio generation contract, text gate, per-card audio QC record, and explicit boundary that TTS audio is not source authenticity evidence.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Trusting declared review scope or legacy status to avoid validating the complete current card object and its self-review metadata snapshot.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Derive changed cards from merge-base to head, require current complete metadata, and compare every metadata field except the independently validated artifact-local review_status.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Allowing a noncanonical card_boxes_json path, unprefixed or template-suffix-disguised governed review path, partial or wrong-track aggregate coverage, full-track remediation coverage for a card absent from merge-base, self-review-only edit, partial base-to-HEAD audit overlay, or legacy text/is_correct shape to bypass the current candidate contract.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Govern every consumed card-box and review path, exclude only exact repository-declared template paths, compare every changed standard self-review entry with its unique HEAD corpus card, count full-track aggregate evidence only when strict internal scope/coverage equals the complete declared track in immutable HEAD and the non-empty track ID set is unchanged from merge-base, materialize the complete immutable HEAD card tree for scoped audit replay, and require explicit runtime IDs on any changed elimination candidate while grandfathering untouched legacy migrations only.

anti_drift_guards.reject: Counting a semantically incomplete, automation-reviewed, nested, symlinked, unusually encoded, current-corpus-drifted, or archived-global-audit-reusing self-review artifact as changed-card coverage; accepting an empty, forged, deleted, renamed, or non-replayed scoped-audit artifact merely because it is unlinked; swapping, truncating, or symlinking standard/full-track authority templates; accepting formal approval with an empty timestamp, summary, scope, or representative evidence; mutating the pre-cutover archive index or one of its named records; forcing unrelated historical scoped reports to refresh whenever the corpus fingerprint changes; or letting candidate-queue or release-gap consumers count templates, traversal, symlinks, incomplete records, historical approvals, dirty/staged/mode-drifted audit authority or approval/review/audit evidence, concurrent HEAD/index/file/corpus drift, forged current-digest audits, stale audits, or stale linked self-reviews as current authorization.
anti_drift_guards.recovery: Require the complete canonical standard or full-track evidence shape before coverage can count, including standard batch progression/risk/representative-card/next-step conclusions; prove exactly three immutable-HEAD-matching snapshots for every declared standard-sample box; compare current review interaction, knowledge, and quality metadata in standalone harness validation; bind every exact regular-file template path and complete placeholder shape to its distinct standard/full-track doc-manifest authority; require valid ISO approval time, non-empty summary, unique non-empty scope arrays, and non-empty unique in-scope representative cards; require a direct current scoped audit for every new or changed review; replay every new or changed scoped report against immutable HEAD even when unlinked, while allowing structurally valid unchanged historical fingerprints and proving hash-pinned legacy exceptions at the active index-introduction commit; freeze the pre-cutover index and complete referenced record bytes against the same commit; forbid residual closure evidence from authorizing newly added cards; use structured human reviewer identities that reject agent and automation tokens; preserve Git paths exactly; reject unsafe path characters and non-regular files; recursively discover nested records so only direct canonical JSON records can pass; and require every current-authorization consumer to validate direct canonical non-template approval and linked review evidence with complete fields and exact current scope, bind those records, both scoped reports, the active audit script, and active audit rule spec to regular committed files whose worktree, index, and one fixed HEAD modes and bytes agree, independently regenerate the complete current card-quality audit, exactly replay both scoped reports, and recheck the fixed HEAD/index snapshot, captured file modes/bytes, and corpus fingerprint before returning.
